easa.q: Name the three axes of an aircraft.
easa.explain: Roll about the longitudinal axis, pitch about the lateral axis, yaw about the vertical axis (EASA p. 4.2).
easa.src: EASA M08 Q4-1 (p. 4.11, answer 4-1 on p. 4.12)

easa.q: Static longitudinal stability of an aircraft depends on what three things?
opts: Wingspan; fuselage length; number of engines
Location of the wing relative to the CG; location of the horizontal tail relative to the CG; area of the tail
Wing location; fuselage shape; paint colour
easa.explain: EASA p. 4.4: all three revolve around the CG because a free body always rotates about its CG.
easa.src: EASA M08 Q4-2 (p. 4.11, answer 4-2 on p. 4.12)

easa.q: An increase in wing ____ increases the lateral stability of the aircraft in flight.
easa.explain: Dihedral is the main means of lateral stability (EASA p. 4.7, Figure 4-9). The printed answer is labelled 4-3 but belongs to question 4-5.
easa.src: EASA M08 Q4-5 (p. 4.11, answer 4-3 on p. 4.12)

easa.q: Stability about the vertical axis of an aircraft is known as ____ or ____ stability.
easa.explain: The printed answer is labelled 4-4 but belongs to question 4-6; the fin governs this stability.
easa.src: EASA M08 Q4-6 (p. 4.11, answer 4-4 on p. 4.12)

etkin.q: The B747 phugoid has eigenvalue λ = −0.003289 ± 0.06723i (units 1/s). The period of the oscillation is:
etkin.explain: T = 2π/ω with ω the imaginary part.
etkin.detail: T = 2π/0.06723 = 93.5 s. Etkin quotes 93 s. Using the real part 0.003289 would give 1910 s, completely wrong.

etkin.q: The B747 short-period mode has λ = −0.3719 ± 0.8875i. The damping ratio ζ = −σ/|λ| is approximately:
The Lanchester approximation T = π√2·u₀/g for the B747 with u₀ = 773.98 ft/s (g = 32.174 ft/s²) gives:
etkin.explain: Lanchester assumes no drag, so it differs from the true 93 s.
etkin.detail: T = π√2 × 773.98/32.174 = 106.9 s (Etkin quotes 107 s). The SI calculation gives the same: u₀ = 235.9 m/s, g = 9.807 m/s² gives 106.9 s.

etkin.q: The B747 characteristic polynomial is λ⁴ + 0.750468λ³ + 0.935494λ² + 0.0094630λ + 0.0041959 = 0. According to Exercise 6.4, the coefficient of λ³ equals:
opts: minus the sum of the real parts of all roots: 0.7505
the sum of the squares of the imaginary parts
the sum of the undamped natural frequencies
etkin.explain: The "sum of the dampings" of the modes.
etkin.detail: −Σ Re λ = 2(0.003289 + 0.3719) = 0.750468 ≈ 0.750468 ✓. That is also why a positive value is necessary for stability.

etkin.q: The time for the B747 phugoid amplitude to halve (t½ = ln 2/|σ|, σ = −0.003289) is:
etkin.detail: t½ = 0.6931/0.003289 = 210.7 s ≈ 2.3 periods. The phugoid decays very slowly, so pilots must watch for it.

etkin.q: In the Lanchester approximation, if the B747 flew at u₀ = 400 ft/s instead of 773.98 ft/s the phugoid period would be about:
etkin.explain: T is directly proportional to speed.
etkin.detail: T = π√2 × 400/32.174 = 55.2 s. Unlike many aerodynamic quantities, T scales with speed, not speed squared.

generated.q: An aircraft has its CG at h = 0.25 and neutral point h_n = 0.35 (in MAC fractions). The static margin K_n is:
generated.explain: K_n = h_n − h = 0.10; positive, hence stable.

generated.q: Moving the CG aft to exactly the neutral point makes C_mα:
generated.explain: C_mα = C_Lα(h − h_n) = 0 when h = h_n (Etkin 2.3).

An oscillation whose initial tendency is to return but whose amplitude then grows over time shows:
opts: negative static and positive dynamic stability
positive static but negative dynamic stability
generated.explain: The initial tendency to return is static positive; amplitude growing in time is dynamic negative (EASA p. 4.3).

a larger effective angle of attack so its lift increases
